paper.title: Stochastic Linear Bandits with Hidden Low Rank Structure

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandit (SLB) with hidden low-dimensional subspace structure in the actions
unmapped: Each round's decision set has K random actions x_hat = x + psi where the true actions x lie in an unknown m-dimensional subspace span(V) (m <= d) and psi is isotropic zero-mean perturbation with covariance sigma_pert^2 I_d, uncorrelated with x; decision sets are random (stochastic), not adversarial
Bounded action and perturbation vectors: ||x||^2 <= d_x lambda_+, ||psi||^2 <= d_psi sigma_pert^2 (Assumption 1)
The learner knows the subspace dimension m, lambda_+ and lambda_- (largest/m-th eigenvalue of Sigma_x), the perturbation variance sigma^2, and alpha = max(d_x, d_psi)
Unlabelled actions in the decision sets are used for PCA subspace recovery
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t \in [T]$, the agent is given a decision set $D_t$ with $K$ actions, $\hat{x}_{t,1}, \ldots, \hat{x}_{t,K} \in \mathbb{R}^d$. Let $V$ be an $d \times m$ orthonormal matrix with $m \leq d$ ... $\hat{x}_{t,i} = x_{t,i} + \psi_{t,i}$ ... $r_t = (P\hat{X}_t)^T \theta_* + \eta_t$ ... $\theta_* \in \spn(V)$

symbols.alpha_eff: max(d_x, d_psi), effective dimensions of true actions and perturbations
symbols.Gamma: 2 g_psi + 4 sqrt(g_x g_psi), with g_x = lambda_plus/lambda_minus, g_psi = sigma_pert^2/lambda_minus
symbols.lambda_plus: largest eigenvalue of the true-action covariance
symbols.lambda_minus: m-th eigenvalue of the true-action covariance
symbols.sigma_pert: standard deviation of the isotropic action perturbation

conditions: x_hat^T theta_* in [-1,1] for all actions

source.label: RegretAnalysis
source.quote: Fix any $\delta \in (0,1/6)$. Assume that Assumptions 1 and 2 hold. Also assume that for all $\hat{x}_{t,i} \in D_t$, $\hat{x}_{t,i}^T \theta_* \in [-1,1]$. Then, $\forall t \geq 1$ with probability at least $1-6\delta$, the regret of \alg satisfies $R_t \leq \min \Big \lbrace \wt\OO\left(\Upsilon \sqrt{t}\right) , \wt\OO\left(d \sqrt{t}\right)\Big\rbrace.$

results.notes: Holds with prob. >= 1-6delta for all t. The proof yields O(Upsilon sqrt(t) log t) for the projected part; the d sqrt(t) part comes from intersecting with OFUL's confidence set. Regret is the realized sum of (X*_t - X_t)^T theta_* against the per-round best action. Optimistic step requires a joint argmax over confidence sets (computationally hard per the paper).
